title: Faceless Void Control

sources.label: ENDGAME Rank Up ★★★ FACLESS Build For Dota Auto Chess

body:
# Faceless Void Control

This is a legendary-heavy control board built on a two-unit foundation: pairing
Faceless Void with Bane activates the Faceless species bond, which makes your
entire team immune to crowd control. From there you don't chase a wide synergy —
you stack the strongest crowd-control legendaries in the game (Tidehunter,
Primal Beast, Queen of Pain, Techies, Snapfire) and let them chain stuns, hexes
and area damage into an enemy team that can't do the same back to you. The catch
is that Faceless immunity is the *only* bond you want lit up, so every other unit
you add has to be picked so it never completes a second species or class — a
"pure Faceless" board rather than a synergy stack. It's weak in the early game
and only comes online once you hit level 9 and start finding tier-five units,
but by the mid game it counters almost everything except raw stat-check comps
like nine warriors.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Faceless Void | 2 | Assassin, Faceless | Half of the CC-immunity bond — keep on board all game |
| Bane | 1 | Faceless, Satyr, Warlock | The other half of the Faceless bond; fears the front line |
| Tidehunter | 5 | Hunter, Naga | Primary carry — a giant AoE stun that always lands, doubled by Refresher Orb |
| Primal Beast | 5 | Beast, Warrior | Frontline lockdown; grabs and pins enemies (dislikes Refresher — it has a cast time) |
| Queen of Pain | 5 | Assassin, Demon | Backline burst and pure damage from the single-Demon trait |
| Techies | 5 | Goblin, Mech | Bomb burst that can one-shot clusters; devastating with Refresher Orb |
| Snapfire | 4 | Goblin, Knight | Armor-shredding single-target damage; the main 3-star target |
| Phoenix | 4 | Elemental, Mage | Sustain and damage-over-time; hard to interrupt because it inherits Faceless immunity |
| Doom | 4 | Demon, Warrior | Optional lockdown, and a second Demon so the Demon bond stays *off* |

Because the board must stay "pure Faceless," treat each addition as a singleton:
two Assassins (Void + Queen of Pain) is fine since Assassin needs three, and if
you want to run Doom you *must* have a second Demon on board so the Demon trait
doesn't accidentally activate. Anti-Mage and Monkey King are reasonable extra
purple bodies with the same "no duplicate synergy" logic.

## Items

Itemization is the second half of the build, and two tier-four items carry it:
**Refresher Orb** and **Minotaur Horn**. Refresher Orb is the standout — put it
on a big-cast caster like Tidehunter or Techies and they cast their game-ending
spell twice per fight. It's wasted on Primal Beast, whose ability has a long
cast time. Minotaur Horn guarantees the unit is at full mana to cast instantly
when the fight opens. **Dagon** is a fine secondary for extra burst on Techies,
and **Satanic** keeps Snapfire alive as it dives. Early tier-one/two items are
just stepping stones — hold **Sliver** to combine upward and don't reroll for
low-tier items when players start dying and dropping free loot after round 25.

## Relics

Everything about the early game is economy, so prioritize relics that fund the
fast climb to level 9. **Malefic Rapture** rewards the losing streak this build
runs, **Magic Seed** is a strong flat economy boost, and the win-streak
protector (Chiaroscuro Certainty) is worth it if you flip to winning. Skip
**March of The Beasts** — the doubled neutral waves are hard to clear with an
undeveloped board. **Second Chance** helps if you're leaning on the item forge,
since the build wants purple items.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

The defining trick is that this is a fast level-9 build. Run a losing streak in
the early game with two Priests down before round 4 for the best income, and
keep three Humans on the board through the mid game — the 3-Human bonus fuels
rapid leveling. Around round 10 you should be level 5 and able to clear the
golems. At round 20, sell your fillers, push to level 9, and start rolling for
tier-five control units — this is your stabilization window from rounds 21–25.
Hitting a two-star tier-five unit (an egg-hatched Tidehunter is ideal) is the
single biggest power jump. After round 30, go to level 10 for more purple-unit
odds; three-starring tier-five units is possible but not required. Dismissing
Humans once you're past them boosts your purple-unit rate (though not your
legendary rate), so only do it with surplus gold.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Space your units out so they each absorb some damage and reach full mana to
guarantee their casts, rather than clumping where one AoE wipes several at once.
Keep Bane and Primal Beast forward to bait and pin the enemy front line, with
Tidehunter positioned to land its stun across the whole enemy team before the
backline casters (Techies, Snapfire, Queen of Pain) follow up. Because you're
immune to crowd control, most comps simply can't stop your casts — the build is
a natural counter to anything that relies on debuffs, including Beast/"savage"
boards. The real threats are stat-check comps that don't need to disable you:
nine warriors (pure armor and damage reflection) and nine assassins (pure
damage) can out-muscle you, so tech in a pure-damage answer like a heavy hammer
item against heavily armored boards.
